tailored_cv.summary: This CV is both a working example and an open application. I combine technology and innovation management with strategy and finance – evidenced by GenAI at CENVION, decision analysis for Swisscom and Airbus, and experience across M&A, banking and consulting. If that profile fits a problem you need solved, let's talk. To adapt it: target profile | differentiation | two evidenced results | value offered.

paragraphs: Some cover letters begin with enthusiasm for one particular vacancy. This one begins more honestly: I am looking for a role that connects innovation management and technology with strategy and finance – while ccvl demonstrates how I structure applications like this one.

At CENVION, I introduced Claude and RAG-based search into investment and reporting workflows. At Airbus, I translated more than 20 years of safety-critical data into risk and cost signals; at Swisscom, I modelled cloud economics and infrastructure decisions. Technology matters most to me when it improves real decisions.

The commercial side is part of the same picture: project-finance and M&A models, eight-figure infrastructure investments, CHF 10m+ supplier negotiations, and end-to-end project P&L in my own consulting work. I can build a prototype and explain why it is worth building.

That does not produce a perfectly linear specialist profile – fortunately. It produces someone who understands emerging technology hands-on, frames its strategic relevance, and carries it into delivery with a sound business case. The more interesting problems tend to live at exactly those intersections.

If your team needs someone who does more than put innovation on slides – someone who analyses it, builds it, and translates it commercially – we should talk. If you came for the template instead: fork it, insert your own facts, verify every claim, and the next strong cover letter is yours.
